papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals a T Cell-Mediated Microglial Activation Axis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibition-Related Adverse Events in the Brain.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting CTLA-4 and PD-1 have transformed cancer therapy, yet their immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in various tissues, including the brain, remain poorly defined. ICI perturbs hippocampal-dependent memory function by derailing neuro-immune homeostasis and compromising synaptic integrity. However, the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which ICI alters regional interactions are not well understood. Using bulk RNA-sequencing and MERFISH spatial transcriptomics in a syngeneic murine melanoma model, we show that ICI treatment remodels hippocampal gene
papers.summary: Using bulk RNA-seq and MERFISH spatial transcriptomics in a mouse melanoma model, this study maps how immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy disrupts hippocampal neuro-immune homeostasis, revealing a T cell-mediated microglial activation axis underlying cognitive side effects. The findings link peripheral ICI treatment to regional brain immune crosstalk and synaptic impairment, offering a mechanistic framework for ICI-related adverse events in the brain.

papers.title: Machine learning and computational approaches to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma.
papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) remains one of the most lethal cancers affecting children, adolescents and young adults and is near-universally resistant to treatment. Histone H3-alterations establish a profoundly dysregulated epigenetic landscape that promotes extensive intratumoral heterogeneity and cellular plasticity, key drivers of therapeutic resistance and treatment failure. Although single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have transformed the study of tumor evolution, the mechanisms underpinning treatment resistance in DMG remain poorly understood. This Review examines how
papers.summary: This review examines how machine learning and computational approaches can be used to model therapeutic response and resistance in diffuse midline glioma (DMG), a lethal pediatric brain cancer driven by histone H3 alterations and epigenetic dysregulation. It highlights how single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics are transforming the study of tumor evolution and resistance mechanisms in DMG. The review discusses computational strategies for integrating these data to better understand and predict treatment failure.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial mapping reveals reproducible cell type organization and spatially dependent gene expression in gastruloids.
papers.abstract: Gastruloids are stem-cell-based models that recapitulate key aspects of mammalian gastrulation, including the formation of an anterior-posterior axis. However, we do not have detailed spatial information about gene expression and cell type organization, particularly at the level of individual gastruloids. Here, we report a spatially resolved, single-cell molecular catalog of the transcriptomes of 26 individual gastruloids. We found that cell type composition and tissue-scale spatial organization were largely consistent across gastruloids, but meso-scale patterning of specific cell types varied
papers.summary: This study provides a spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic atlas of 26 individual gastruloids, stem-cell-based models of mammalian gastrulation. It shows that overall cell type composition and tissue-scale spatial organization are highly reproducible across gastruloids, while meso-scale patterning of specific cell types is more variable. The work establishes a detailed molecular catalog linking spatial position to gene expression in these embryo-like structures.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomic analysis of neurons at the glioma infiltration front: A case study.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics reveals localized IGFBP5 expression and TGFβ-related signaling in neurons within glioma-infiltrated tissue.
papers.summary: This case study uses spatial transcriptomics to examine neurons at the infiltration front of glioma, revealing localized expression of IGFBP5 and activation of TGFβ-related signaling pathways in neurons within glioma-infiltrated tissue. The findings suggest that neurons in the tumor microenvironment undergo region-specific molecular changes that may influence glioma progression.

papers.title: Spatially resolved single cell atlas deciphers SAA1 inflammatory epithelial cells.
papers.abstract: Disruption of epithelial integrity is a pivotal event in inflammation, disease pathogenesis, and tissue homeostasis. To investigate these processes in chronic inflammatory disease, we performed spatial transcriptomics integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on human gingival tissue, coupled with metagenomic analysis of matched subgingival plaque. This approach allowed in situ characterization of epithelial heterogeneity and microbiome-epithelium-connective tissue crosstalk. We identified a distinct inflammatory epithelial subpopulation (SAA1+Epi), situated within the junctional
papers.summary: This study combined spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and metagenomic analysis of matched subgingival plaque to characterize epithelial heterogeneity and microbiome-epithelium-connective tissue crosstalk in human gingival tissue. The authors identified a distinct inflammatory epithelial subpopulation marked by SAA1 (SAA1+Epi) located within the junctional epithelium, linking microbial signals to epithelial inflammatory states in chronic inflammatory disease.

papers.title: Spatial cell-cell communication inference based on cell-spot-ligand-receptor heterogeneous graphs.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication is essential for tissue homeostasis and disease-associated microenvironment remodeling. Spatial transcriptomics enables the study of communication events in situ, but single-cell-resolution inference from spot-based data remains challenging because of uncertain cell-to-spot mapping, limited use of local spatial information, and false positives from ligand-receptor co-expression. Existing methods increasingly emphasize spatial proximity in cell-cell communication inference, while integrating biologically informative signals remains important for improving the interpretab
papers.summary: The authors present a computational method that infers cell-cell communication from spot-based spatial transcriptomics data by modeling cell-spot-ligand-receptor relationships as a heterogeneous graph. This approach addresses key challenges such as uncertain cell-to-spot mapping and false positives from ligand-receptor co-expression, improving the accuracy and interpretability of spatial communication inference.

papers.title: The Polycystic Kidney Disease Cyst Transcriptome Defined by Integrating Spatial, Single Nuclear, and Bulk Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) has been transcriptionally profiled at single cellular resolution, yet dissociation eliminated cyst-defining morphology to preclude a retrograde analysis of the cyst transcriptome. Transcriptional profiling of dissected ADPKD cysts has demonstrated size-based transcriptional heterogeneity, impossible to define in prior single cell analysis, but sampling was neither single cell nor comprehensive to limit downstream transcriptional analysis.
papers.summary: This study integrates spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-seq, and bulk RNA-seq to characterize the transcriptome of cysts in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). By combining these approaches, the authors overcome limitations of prior single-cell studies that lost cyst morphology during dissociation and of bulk cyst profiling that lacked single-cell resolution. The resulting cyst transcriptome provides a more comprehensive view of transcriptional heterogeneity within ADPKD cysts.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics Reveals Cellular States and Microenvironmental Remodeling in Coexisting DCIS and IDC.
papers.abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is a non-invasive precursor of invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), yet the biological mechanisms underlying the transition from DCIS to IDC remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrate spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and single-cell DNA sequencing on coexisting DCIS and IDC samples to characterize cellular and microenvironmental alterations. Integrated analyses reveal differential molecular characterizations between coexisting DCIS and IDC and identify candidate genes (MGP, PLAT, and SERPINA3) potentially limiting the progression from DCI
papers.summary: This study integrates spatial transcriptomics, single-cell RNA sequencing, and single-cell DNA sequencing to compare coexisting DCIS and IDC lesions within the same patients. It identifies distinct molecular and microenvironmental differences between the two stages and nominates MGP, PLAT, and SERPINA3 as candidate genes that may restrain progression from DCIS to invasive disease.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using S
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to characterize cell adhesion-related gene expression patterns in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identify cell adhesion gene signatures that may serve as therapeutic targets for reducing inflammatory infiltration and preserving blood-brain barrier integrity after stroke.

papers.title: Wnt/β-catenin reduces fibrosis and enhances hepatocyte reprogramming during cholestasis independent of Yap signaling.
papers.abstract: Cholestatic liver diseases are characterized by impaired bile flow. Repairing damage and reestablishing biliary function may slow disease progression and reduce complications. The Wnt/β-catenin pathway can facilitate biliary repair during cholestasis through multiple mechanisms. The impact of constitutive Wnt/β-catenin signaling during cholestasis was analyzed using S45D transgenic (TG) mice, which express non-degradable β-catenin. Compared to WT, TG mice had increased inflammation and decreased fibrosis during prolonged cholestasis. Furthermore, TG mice had increased ductular reaction and hep
papers.summary: Using transgenic mice expressing a non-degradable form of β-catenin, this study shows that constitutive Wnt/β-catenin signaling during cholestasis increases inflammation and ductular reaction while reducing liver fibrosis and promoting hepatocyte reprogramming. These effects occur independently of Yap signaling, suggesting Wnt/β-catenin as a potential therapeutic target for cholestatic liver disease.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: The authors introduce crumblr, a scalable statistical method for analyzing cell type composition changes in single-cell data. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs and count ratio data. This enables fast, flexible identification of cell type frequency differences across large cohorts.

papers.title: Decoding Skeletal Biology Through Transcriptomics: Insights from Bulk, Single-Cell, Spatial, and Multi-Omics Approaches.
papers.abstract: Transcriptomic technologies have revolutionized our understanding of skeletal biology by shifting research from descriptive cellular characterization to a systems-level analysis of bone homeostasis and pathology. The rapid evolution of bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and integrative multi-omics approaches has enabled unprecedented resolution of the molecular and cellular complexity of the skeletal microenvironment. Bone remodeling is a tightly regulated process driven by coordinated interactions among bone marrow-derived mese
papers.summary: This review surveys how transcriptomic technologies—bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multi-omics integration—have transformed skeletal biology research from descriptive cell characterization to systems-level analysis of bone homeostasis and pathology. It highlights how these approaches resolve the molecular and cellular complexity of the skeletal microenvironment, including the coordinated interactions driving bone remodeling.

papers.title: Next-Generation Biomarkers and Artificial Intelligence in Colorectal Cancer: From Multi-Omic Data Integration to Clinical Application.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, although advances in molecular profiling and artificial intelligence (AI) are now reshaping precision oncology in ways that promise better patient outcomes. This review synthesises contemporary evidence on next-generation biomarkers and AI applications in CRC across multi-omic data integration, liquid biopsy, computational pathology, radiomics and clinical implementation. Several findings stand out. Integrated multi-omic approaches combining genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and microbiomic
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on next-generation biomarkers and artificial intelligence applications in colorectal cancer, covering multi-omic data integration, liquid biopsy, computational pathology, and radiomics. It highlights how combining genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and microbiome data with AI is reshaping precision oncology for CRC. The review also addresses clinical implementation challenges and opportunities.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Analysis Identifies TTYH3 and MPG as Candidate Osteoporosis-Associated Biomarkers in Osteoblasts and Characterizes Spatial Heterogeneity of SPP1 in the Osteoporotic Bone Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Background: Osteoporosis (OP) arises from dysregulated bone metabolism driven by genetic and epigenetic factors. Osteoblasts are central to bone formation, and their functional heterogeneity-shaped by genetic background and receptor expression profiles-may critically influence OP susceptibility. This study aimed to identify osteoblast-specific genes robustly associated with OP and elucidate their underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Methods: We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq), and spatial transcriptomics (ST) datasets of osteoblasts. Differentia
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to identify osteoblast-specific genes associated with osteoporosis, nominating TTYH3 and MPG as candidate biomarkers. It also characterizes spatial heterogeneity of SPP1 within the osteoporotic bone microenvironment, highlighting how osteoblast functional diversity may contribute to disease susceptibility.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies Epithelial-Stromal-Immune Co-Regulators Bridging Ulcerative Colitis and Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) carry a substantially elevated risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC); yet, the transcriptional intermediates that bridge chronic mucosal inflammation and colorectal malignancy remain poorly characterized. A related question is whether any genes shared between the two conditions actually help drive transformation, or whether they represent downstream responders. Methods: We integrated two UC microarray cohorts (totalling 227 samples) and the TCGA-COAD dataset (n = 524), combining weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCN
papers.summary: This study integrated transcriptomic data from ulcerative colitis (UC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) cohorts using weighted gene co-expression network analysis to identify shared epithelial-stromal-immune regulatory modules that may bridge chronic inflammation and malignancy. The analysis highlights co-regulators that could serve as mechanistic links or biomarkers for UC-associated colorectal cancer. The work is primarily computational and identifies candidate pathways for further experimental validation.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper introduces a real-data-driven framework for benchmarking differential transcript usage (DTU) detection methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. Unlike prior evaluations that rely mainly on simulated data, this framework uses real biological data to assess method performance, aiming to reduce bias and better reflect true regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: From Glycan Biology to Drug Candidates: An Integrated Sialylation Niche Index and AI-Guided Therapeutic Framework for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) responds poorly (<20%) to immune checkpoint blockade. Since sialylation suppresses anti-tumour immunity through Siglec signalling independently of the PD-L1/PD-1 axis, we mapped its prognostic landscape in HNSCC by integrating prognostic modelling, molecular subtyping, and AI-guided drug discovery. Methods: Transcriptomic data from seven GEO cohorts and TCGA-HNSC (n = 501) were analysed with a 1204-gene sialylation compendium. The Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) was built in TCGA-HNSC from 117 machine-learning algorithm combinations (nomi
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data from multiple HNSCC cohorts to build a Sialylation Niche Index (SNI) using machine-learning combinations, linking sialylation-related gene expression to prognosis and immune checkpoint blockade resistance. The authors then use AI-guided drug discovery to propose therapeutic candidates targeting the sialylation niche in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.

papers.title: Genotype-driven tumor ecosystems drive immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in melanoma.
papers.abstract: Genetic and transcriptional alterations in cancer cells shape their interactions with immune and stromal compartments, thereby influencing tumor progression, immune evasion, and response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Yet, how these interactions are spatially organized within melanoma and how they relate to clinical outcome remains incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study examines how genetic and transcriptional changes in melanoma cells shape their spatial interactions with immune and stromal cells within the tumor ecosystem, and how these interactions contribute to immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors. The authors aim to link the spatial organization of these genotype-driven tumor ecosystems to clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to 1-nitropyrene, a diesel exhaust pollutant, causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice. By combining single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with a machine-learning algorithm, the authors pinpoint extravillous trophoblasts as the key cell type affected and identify core regulatory targets driving the dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses genetic multiplexing to profile transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain, revealing cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics. It verifies and extends prior single-cell RNA-seq findings, showing that molecular subtypes of circadian neurons correspond to distinct connectomic subtypes. The work provides a higher-resolution view of how individual neuron types within the circadian network respond to time of day and light.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell, Spatial, and Bulk Transcriptomics Characterizes an Outcome-Associated, Spatially Organized Mesenchymal Program in IDH-Mutant Glioma.
papers.abstract: IDH-mutant gliomas show variable clinical behavior that may reflect transcriptional programs organized within tumor tissue. We evaluated two curated expression scores: a differentiation-loss/Stem-NPC score (Axis1) and a mesenchymal-hypoxia score (Axis2). Public single-cell RNA-sequencing data were used to characterize malignant-cell states, and the scores were evaluated in bulk clinical cohorts using portable within-sample ranks and covariate-adjusted Cox models. Axis2 was separated into non-overlapping mesenchymal-only and hypoxia-only components. Spatial organization was tested in Visium sec
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell, spatial, and bulk transcriptomics to identify a mesenchymal-hypoxia transcriptional program in IDH-mutant gliomas that is spatially organized within tumor tissue and associated with patient outcomes. By separating mesenchymal and hypoxia components, the authors show that the mesenchymal program specifically correlates with clinical behavior, suggesting it could serve as a prognostic biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: Layer-Resolved Spatial Transcriptomic Profiling Reveals Distinct Fibrotic and Muscularizing Submucosal Niches in Fibrostenotic Crohn's Disease.
papers.abstract: Fibrostenotic stricture is a severe complication of Crohn's disease (CD) that affect up to 50% of patients over their lifetime, causing irreversible narrowing of the intestinal lumen and bowel obstruction, but the molecular programs that distinguish stenotic from non-stenotic inflammation and the relative contributions of fibrosis and smooth-muscle remodeling remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to dissect bowel-wall compartment-specific and histology-defined remodeling programs in fibrostenotic CD.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint uses layer-resolved spatial transcriptomics to map gene expression across the bowel wall in fibrostenotic Crohn's disease, distinguishing stenotic from non-stenotic inflammation. The authors identify distinct submucosal niches characterized by either fibrotic or smooth-muscle remodeling programs, helping clarify the relative contributions of fibrosis versus muscularization to stricture formation.

papers.title: Multiscale Transcriptomic and Molecular Modeling Analyses Suggest DCPMU-Associated Epithelial Remodeling and Tumor Microenvironment Perturbation in Prostate Cancer.
papers.abstract: DCPMU, a major demethylated metabolite of diuron, is an environmentally persistent contaminant with potential endocrine-disrupting and carcinogenic relevance, yet its mechanistic association with prostate cancer remains unclear. This study investigated DCPMU-related mechanisms in prostate cancer by integrating network toxicology, molecular modeling, bulk transcriptomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and virtual perturbation analysis. Differentially expressed genes from TCGA-PRAD were intersected with DCPMU-associated and prostate cancer-related targets. Functional enrichment, machi
papers.summary: This study integrates network toxicology, molecular modeling, bulk and single-cell/spatial transcriptomics to investigate how DCPMU, a persistent environmental metabolite of the herbicide diuron, may contribute to prostate cancer. The authors identify DCPMU-associated gene signatures linked to epithelial remodeling and tumor microenvironment perturbation, suggesting a mechanistic link between this contaminant and prostate cancer progression.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses of epigenomic variation.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their target genes also oscillate, avoiding the need for costly and time-consuming bioluminescence imaging of each target individually. The tool leverages existing gene expression data to reconstruct oscillation patterns, offering a scalable way to study Notch-driven ultradian rhythms in processes like progenitor fate decisions.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors present a meta-classifier that arbitrates disagreements between ten gene regulatory network inference methods on a per-edge basis, using the raw scores each method assigns to candidate regulator-target pairs as features for a gradient-boosted classifier. They also propose a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. This approach moves beyond choosing a single method or simple averaging, allowing method weighting to vary edge by edge.

papers.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Prioritization of Candidate Drug Targets in Tumors Using Spatial Multi-Omics.
papers.abstract: Tumor heterogeneity is reflected in cell composition, molecular states, spatial distribution, and microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics can map in situ expression and cell states but cannot fully explain upstream regulation, while spatial epigenomics provides complementary evidence such as chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) methylation. This review summarizes the applications of spatial multi-omics and deep learning in prioritizing candidate drug targets in tumors.
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics) can be combined with deep learning to identify and prioritize candidate drug targets in tumors. It argues that integrating complementary spatial layers—gene expression, chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and DNA methylation—provides a more complete picture of tumor heterogeneity and upstream regulation than any single modality. The authors survey current applications and outline how deep learning can help extract target candidates from these complex spatial datasets.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of TIMP1-associated stromal-myeloid remodeling in autoimmune gastritis and gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune gastritis (AIG) is a chronic immune-mediated atrophic disease that can induce cancer-related epithelial remodeling, although its association with gastric adenocarcinoma depends on histological and clinical modifiers. Gastric cancer (GC) progression is shaped by the tumor microenvironment (TME), including cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), myeloid cells, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Whether AIG-related mucosal remodeling shares stromal programs with GC-associated stromal-myeloid niches remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to compare the stromal and myeloid cell programs in autoimmune gastritis (AIG) and gastric cancer (GC), focusing on the role of TIMP1 in remodeling the tissue microenvironment. The authors find that AIG-related mucosal remodeling shares stromal-myeloid niche features with GC, suggesting a potential link between chronic autoimmune inflammation and cancer-associated microenvironmental changes.

papers.title: Ferroptosis Signatures in Diabetic Cardiomyopathy: Multi-Omics Discovery and Validation of ACOT1 and TXNIP.
papers.abstract: Background: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a serious cardiovascular complication specific to diabetes mellitus, with rising global prevalence. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lethal lipid peroxidation, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of DCM. However, the key regulatory genes remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify and validate ferroptosis-related signature genes in DCM. Methods: Three murine transcriptomic datasets (GSE123975, GSE155377, and GSE210611) were retrieved from GEO and merged after batch correction. Differentially exp
papers.summary: This study integrated three mouse transcriptomic datasets to identify ferroptosis-related genes involved in diabetic cardiomyopathy, pinpointing ACOT1 and TXNIP as key signature genes. The findings were validated experimentally, suggesting these genes may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets for this diabetes complication.

papers.title: Integrating Next-Generation Reproductive Organoids with Genomics, Multi-Omics and Bioengineering to Understand Human Infertility.
papers.abstract: Infertility affects approximately one in six individuals worldwide and is a highly heterogeneous disorder resulting from the complex interplay of genetic, epigenetic, endocrine, environmental and lifestyle factors. Although numerous genes and molecular pathways involved in female and male infertility have been identified, elucidating the functional consequences of disease-associated variants remains challenging due to the lack of relevant human experimental models. In recent years, reproductive organoids have emerged as powerful three-dimensional systems that recapitulate key structural, cellu
papers.summary: This review discusses how next-generation reproductive organoids—three-dimensional stem-cell-derived models of reproductive tissues—can be combined with genomics, multi-omics, and bioengineering approaches to study human infertility. The authors argue that these integrated platforms help overcome the limitations of traditional models by allowing functional interrogation of infertility-associated genetic variants and the complex gene-environment interactions underlying the disorder.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to investigate lactylation-related gene signatures in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI). Using five gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors identify lactylation-associated genes that may contribute to HIRI pathogenesis. The findings suggest that lactate metabolism and lactylation play a role in HIRI and could serve as potential therapeutic targets or biomarkers.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer, identifying epithelial cell-derived genes that predict survival and immunotherapy response. Low-PIS patients show better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 is validated as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing with machine learning to analyze ovarian cancer samples, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor clinical outcomes. The findings suggest that these inflammatory and fibroblast populations contribute to residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, highlighting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue structure and protein markers, enabling immunohistochemical analysis of pigmented eye tissues in mice. Using this method, they created a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye, tracking markers like Rpe65, Rhodopsin, and Dct across development. They also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets to complement the spatial findings.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets (over 434,000 cells), introducing a Biological Discordance Score (BDS) to quantify how marker gene interpretation varies across pipelines. The authors find that the choice of normalization method affects biological interpretation more strongly than the choice of clustering algorithm, highlighting a critical source of analytical variability in single-cell cancer studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This paper investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbiota and their metabolites migrate to the intervertebral disc microenvironment and contribute to disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify key microbes and molecular mechanisms mediating this cross-kingdom migration, though the abstract does not yet report specific findings.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The analysis suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The findings are computational and hypothesis-generating, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood to identify NETosis-associated gene programs and a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in patients with severe acute pancreatitis. The findings suggest these blood-based signatures could help distinguish severe-spectrum disease and potentially flag patients at risk of persistent organ failure.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework for large-scale scRNA-seq data that combines a fast Louvain algorithm for initial cluster generation with a Transformer-based model to refine clustering. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing methods when handling large-scale single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Single-cell-informed senescence programs underpin a machine-learning prognostic model robustly validated across melanoma cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) shapes tumor evolution and the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet senescence-informed prognostic models for skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a robust senescence-related prognostic signature by integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data with systematic machine-learning screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify cellular senescence programs in skin cutaneous melanoma and uses machine-learning screening to build a senescence-related prognostic signature. The resulting model is validated across multiple independent melanoma cohorts, suggesting senescence-informed signatures can robustly stratify patient outcomes.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify NK cell-related hub genes and build a two-gene risk model for COPD. The model is proposed as a potential diagnostic tool, addressing the limited availability of NK cell-based markers for this disease.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific immune cell program—JAML+ lipid-associated macrophages—that shows high transcriptome-wide association activity. By combining single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche mapping, and machine learning-based selection, the authors link genetic susceptibility to a pathogenic macrophage state in the diseased liver. The work provides a framework for identifying cell-type-specific therapeutic targets in PSC.

papers.title: An integrated network toxicology and multi-omics framework prioritizes BRCA1 as a testable candidate in benzo[a]pyrene-associated oral cancer.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposure to benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) is a recognized risk factor for oral cancer, but systematic strategies for prioritizing candidate molecular nodes and generating experimentally testable hypotheses remain limited. Here, we conducted a hypothesis-generating, methodologically oriented exploratory study using an integrated three-tier framework comprising computational target prioritization, multi-omics contextualization, and preliminary phenotypic assessment. Network toxicology identified four genes shared between the predefined BaP-associated and oral cancer-related gene sets: EGFR,
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated framework combining network toxicology, multi-omics analysis, and preliminary phenotypic experiments to identify candidate genes linking benzo[a]pyrene exposure to oral cancer. The analysis prioritized BRCA1 as a testable candidate among genes shared between BaP-associated and oral cancer gene sets, including EGFR. The work is explicitly hypothesis-generating and methodologically oriented rather than confirmatory.

papers.title: Spatial, single-nucleus and pathological profiling of the invasive front in early hepatocellular carcinoma for characterizing specific leading-edge cell niche and improving recurrence modeling.
papers.abstract: The tumor leading edge (TLE) is a critical region where tumor cells interact with the microenvironment to drive invasion and metastasis; however, its cellular architecture in early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and computational pathology to investigate TLE in early HCC. We annotated 35 cell subpopulations and identified STMN1-high tumor cells as a key malignant subset enriched at the invasive front, interacting with Treg, plasma B, LAMP3⁺ dendritic cells and SPP1⁺ macrophages. Spatial
papers.summary: This study integrates single-nucleus RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and computational pathology to characterize the tumor leading edge (TLE) in early hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors identify 35 cell subpopulations and pinpoint STMN1-high tumor cells as a key malignant subset enriched at the invasive front, interacting with specific immune populations including Tregs, plasma B cells, LAMP3+ dendritic cells, and SPP1+ macrophages. This multi-modal profiling reveals a distinct leading-edge cell niche that improves recurrence modeling.

papers.title: A Hypoxia Associated STC2 High Endothelial Subpopulation is Linked to Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming, Pathological Angiogenesis, and Immune Remodeling in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia drives malignant advancement and immune escape in HNSCC, but its cell‑type‑specific regulatory circuitry within the TME remains insufficiently elucidated. This study systematically characterizes hypoxia‑associated molecular programs and identifies core genes with relevance to prognosis and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This study characterizes hypoxia-associated molecular programs in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying a STC2-high endothelial subpopulation linked to lipid metabolic reprogramming, pathological angiogenesis, and immune remodeling. The findings highlight cell-type-specific hypoxia responses within the tumor microenvironment that may inform prognosis and therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Poly pipeline: a polyvalent spatial transcriptomics workflow validated across polyploid and diploid organisms.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has emerged as a transformative approach for visualizing tissue landscapes, yet it faces significant challenges regarding data standardization, sparsity, and the analysis of complex genomes, particularly polyploid plants. To address these limitations, we introduce Poly Pipeline, a robust and universal bioinformatic workflow designed to streamline analysis across diverse plant and animal genomes. The pipeline integrates a comprehensive converter for proprietary formats, clustering algorithms, and hdWGCNA co-expression networks, which indirectly preserves the express
papers.summary: The authors present Poly Pipeline, a bioinformatics workflow for spatial transcriptomics that handles data from both polyploid and diploid organisms. It combines format conversion, clustering, and hdWGCNA co-expression network analysis to address issues of data standardization and sparsity, particularly in complex plant genomes.

papers.title: Multiscale characterization of an inflammatory macrophage state associated with an air pollutant-prioritized prognostic signature in gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Air pollutants are implicated in carcinogenesis, but their relevance to gastric cancer (GC) across prognosis, tumor organization and cell behavior remains unclear. We integrated evidence to evaluate pollutant-prioritized GC candidates.
papers.summary: This study integrates air pollutant exposure data with gastric cancer molecular profiling to identify a pollutant-prioritized prognostic gene signature. The authors characterize an inflammatory macrophage state linked to this signature, connecting environmental exposure to tumor microenvironment organization and patient outcomes. The work suggests that air pollutants may shape gastric cancer prognosis through immune cell states.

papers.title: Spatially convergent functional MRI signatures of diabetes and male sex identify genetic vulnerabilities to accelerated brain ageing.
papers.abstract: Age-related cognitive decline results from complex interactions between neuroendocrine and neurometabolic processes that undergo lifelong degradation, yet the mechanisms underlying these interactions remain poorly understood. This study examined the effects of diabetes and sex on functional brain networks across ageing through analysis of two large cohorts (N = 1621 total) using both 3T and 7T functional MRI, complemented by spatial transcriptomic data from over 14 000 genes from six post-mortem brains. Four networks-cingulo-opercular, default mode, salience and lateral somatomotor-exhibited s
papers.summary: This study combined functional MRI from two large cohorts (N=1621) with spatial transcriptomic data from post-mortem brains to show that diabetes and male sex produce convergent changes in specific brain networks (cingulo-opercular, default mode, salience, and lateral somatomotor). These spatial patterns of brain alteration align with genetic vulnerabilities linked to accelerated brain ageing, suggesting that metabolic and sex-related factors interact to shape cognitive decline.

papers.title: Identification and experimental validation of CCL26 as a core comorbid gene and biomarker for atopic dermatitis and allergic asthma via machine learning and multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) and allergic asthma (AA) frequently co-occur and are a core component of the "atopic march." However, the shared molecular mechanisms linking these conditions, as well as the core comorbid genes with diagnostic value, remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning and multi-omics analysis to identify CCL26 as a shared core gene and potential biomarker linking atopic dermatitis and allergic asthma, two conditions that frequently co-occur in the 'atopic march.' The finding was experimentally validated, suggesting CCL26 may serve as a diagnostic marker for these comorbid allergic diseases.

papers.title: Genetic associations link lung cancer liability to brain imaging phenotypes and nominate an FN1-associated tumor-oligodendrocyte program in small-cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis is a major cause of mortality in lung cancer, particularly in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). Whether genetic susceptibility to lung cancer is associated with brain structural and functional traits relevant to metastatic vulnerability remains unclear. We investigated subtype-specific genetic associations with brain imaging phenotypes and explored the biological context of the SCLC-associated white-matter signal.
papers.summary: This study uses genetic association analysis to link lung cancer susceptibility, especially small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), to brain imaging phenotypes, finding a white-matter signal associated with SCLC risk. The authors further nominate an FN1-associated tumor-oligodendrocyte program that may underlie brain metastatic vulnerability in SCLC.
